reader.requirement: At --std 85 a successful OPEN must make the file's record area usable. For an EXTERNAL file connector, every program of the run unit that describes the file must share one record area, whether the programs are contained or separately compiled and whether the records are fixed or RECORD VARYING. A non-external file's area must stay private to its program.

reader.notes: The record area of an EXTERNAL FD is a run-unit cell keyed by the file's externalized name. Out-of-line (variable-length) records get a cell of their own under the same key, so describers in different programs alias one area. No edition is consulted on this path.

refuter.evidence: r02a.cob at --std 85: three separately compiled programs describe one EXTERNAL FD with different record layouts of the same length (A: 01 PIC X(8) plus a second 01 with 9(4)/X(4); B: 01 group X(2)/9(2)/X(4); C: 01 PIC X(8)), as §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR2 requires the same length (cite.py: OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR2, the text is in GR2). Printed B-SEES=AB|EFGH (B sees A's MOVE), A-SEES=1234WXYZ NUM=1234 TXT=WXYZ (A's second 01 sees B's numeric MOVE truncated to 9(2)), C-OPEN=00 / C-READ=1234WXYZ (C's READ fills the one area), A-AFTER-C=1234WXYZ (A sees C's READ), A-CLOSE=00 (A closes the connector C opened). One record area per run unit as GR2 says. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR2 (the text is in GR2).
